title: A passing cargo test leaves nothing in TMPDIR, whatever its name: every test removes its own scratch (kept only when it fails), and a halted gate removes its private directory
prompt:
Read crates/spawn-host/tests/api.rs (`scratch`, `repository`), crates/spawn-host/tests/branches.rs (`Fixture`), crates/spawn-host/tests/runtime_files.rs (`project`), crates/spawn-host/src/git.rs (the tests' `due_merge` and `capped`), crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs (the tests' `world`, `fresh_marks`, and the tests that use them), crates/spawn-cli/src/gate.rs (`PrivateDirectory`, `run_bounded`, `Halt`, `park_for_good`), and every other test that makes scratch under std::env::temp_dir().

The problem. The workspace's tests make their scratch under std::env::temp_dir(), as `spawn-<what>-<pid>` (66 sites name one so), and many never remove it. Measured on 351fb1e6 (2026-11-11, each crate's tests alone, with a fresh TMPDIR each, all passing):
- spawn-host: 117 tests in 14 s, 51 entries left (54 MB): spawn-branches-* x31, spawn-git-* x12, spawn-runtime-* x7, spawn-host-test x1;
- spawn-cli: 715 tests in 115 s, 7 entries left (2 MB): spawn-gate-* x3, spawn-db-own-servers-a/-b, spawn-db-gate-own-servers, spawn-land-push;
- spawn-core, spawn-postgres, spawn-kdf, spawn-jev: none.
On this host, one reviewer's suite TMPDIR held 705 entries (714 MB) after 13 crate-suite runs in ten minutes, and /var/tmp/spawn held 6042 entries (5.3 GB), which the gate's socket scan also walks.
One of them is the product's own: a halted gate (`Halt`, an integrator's drain past its bound) parks its thread for good in `run_bounded`, so the gate's `PrivateDirectory` (spawn-gate-<pid>-<nonce>-<n>, its stdout and stderr) is never dropped and stays in the integrator's TMPDIR. The test `a_halt_kills_the_whole_group_and_returns_nothing` leaves two each run, and /var/tmp/spawn holds 76.

Required behaviour.
(a) Every test's scratch is removed when the test ends. A test that fails may keep its own (for debugging), and says where it is. A scratch shared by several tests of one process is removed once none needs it, or is made per test.
(b) A halted gate removes its private directory before its thread parks: the group is killed already, and nothing reads the directory after.
(c) A `cargo test` whose tests all pass leaves no new entry in its TMPDIR, whatever its name. A scratch renamed (another prefix, a hidden name, a bare temporary directory) is still a scratch left behind. On 351fb1e6 the toolchain itself (cargo, rustc, git, psql, the tests' children) leaves nothing there, so no name is allowed. This holds for every crate, not only the two the scenario runs.
(d) Nothing else changes: the same tests, the same assertions and the same number of tests. Remove only what the test made, never by a pattern over TMPDIR, since another process's scratch may be there.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/054.sh (about 140 s). In the tree under test, it runs `cargo test -p spawn-host -p spawn-cli` once (the build is the gate's), with TMPDIR a fresh empty directory of its own. Then:
- (1) the tests pass (a failing suite cannot be judged for its scratch; the check of the tests reports it);
- (2) nothing is left in that TMPDIR, whatever its name.
It fails with 1 at (2) on 351fb1e6: 58 entries (56 MB) left by a passing run.
Once this is solved, the owner folds the same check into the check of the tests (every crate, every gate) and retires 054.sh. So (c) holds for crates the scenario does not run.

The product reason. Every gate runs the crate suites, and so do the reviewers and the workers. About 55 MB and 54 directories per run add up to gigabytes in days, and every gate's socket scan walks them. A halted integrator also leaves a gate directory behind each time.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
